Hmm — should type_designations include "FMR 53X" (the base model)? The certified type is "model FMR 53X" with various antenna variants. I'd include FMR 53X and the antenna variants. Or list the variants only. The schema says "all type/model identifiers mentioned". I'll include "FMR 53X" plus the antenna types: "FMR 530 DN150", "FMR 530 DN200", "FMR 530 DN250", "FMR 531 Teflon 1,5\" (Rod)", "FMR 533 DN450 (Parabolic)", "FMR 532 DN150", "FMR 532 DN200", "FMR 532 DN250", "FMR 532 DN300".

Note: "type FMR 531 Teflon 1,5" (Rod)" — 1,5" is a size, keep as string. Careful with the quote character in JSON — escape it.

module_designation: "Not applicable"? For R85 level gauge... The schema says module_designation: "Analog load cell" | "Not applicable" | null. If not present, omit or null. Not mentioned → omit.

description: "Automatic level gauge for measuring the level of liquid in storage tanks, model FMR 53X with antennas type ..."

model_family: The cert covers >1 model variant (9 antenna variants of FMR 53X). Should I include model_family? The variants are antenna types. Rule 4 says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant. Yes, 9 variants. family_name: "FMR 53X". models: one entry per variant with model_id.

But do attributes vary per model? No characteristics table given — no numeric data. So model_level characteristics: none. I can still emit model_family with models listed, no attributes.

Actually, hmm — is this a "model family"? The variants differ by antenna type and DN (nominal diameter). I think including model_family with family_name "FMR 53X" and the 9 antenna models is reasonable. Alternatively, skip model_family since no attributes vary. The rule says include ONLY if cert covers >1 model variant — it does cover 9 variants. I'll include it.

model_id values: keep them faithful: "FMR 530 DN150", "FMR 530 DN 200" → normalize to "FMR 530 DN200"? The rule says don't fabricate; normalizing whitespace is fine. I'll use consistent forms: "FMR 530 DN150", "FMR 530 DN200", "FMR 530 DN250", "FMR 531 Teflon 1.5\" (Rod)", "FMR 533 DN450 (Parabolic)", "FMR 532 DN150", "FMR 532 DN200", "FMR 532 DN250", "FMR 532 DN300".

Hmm, decimal rule: convert "1,5" → "1.5"? That's a dimension (1.5 inch Teflon rod). The rule about decimal commas applies to values; in a designation string it's fine to keep "1,5" as-is or convert. I'll keep as "1,5\"" faithful: "FMR 531 Teflon 1,5\" (Rod)". Actually mixing — I'll keep faithful to source.

components: antennas could be considered components? The antennas are types of the radar level gauge transmitter itself — they're antenna variants, not separate sub-assemblies. I could record components with role "antenna" listing the types. Hmm. The cert says "model FMR 53X with antennas type FMR 530 DN150; ...". These are antenna variants integrated into the model. I think listing them as components with role "antenna" and alternatives "OR" could be useful. But they're more like model variants. I'll list them in model_family.models and possibly skip components to avoid duplication. Actually the schema says components: include ONLY if cert names sub-assemblies. The antennas are named sub-assemblies of the gauge. But each variant IS a full gauge model (FMR 530, FMR 531, FMR 532, FMR 533 are different device types). Actually reading again: "model FMR 53X with antennas type FMR 530 DN150; type FMR 530 DN 200; ..." — the FMR 530/531/532/533 are antenna types of model FMR 53X. So model_id could be the antenna designations. I'll go with model_family only.
